items.s: Thousands of teenagers ____ lessons for a very different reason.

tfn.s: Every parent and teacher supported the student protests.
tfn.why: The text says the opposite: "Some parents and teachers supported the students, while others worried that staying away from lessons would make learning even harder."

tfn.s: The government agreed to send in more replacement teachers.
tfn.why: The text says: "The French government said it would send in thousands of extra replacement teachers to schools that needed them."

tfn.s: According to the government, over 160,000 people took part on 13 October.
tfn.why: The text says: "More than 160,000 people joined them, according to government figures, although the organisers gave a higher number."

tfn.s: The protests have already led to new school buildings.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not say whether any new school buildings have been built.

tfn.s: Students say they want expensive new equipment for their schools.
tfn.why: The text says: "Many of them say they are not asking for luxury, only for lessons that actually take place."

pre.d: events where many people walk or gather in public to show what they think
the people who work in a place
doors or gates where you go in
fights or angry arguments between groups
plans for how much money you will spend
having more money
a person who does a job instead of someone else
something difficult that you must try to do

focus.note: Some words go together naturally. Learn the pair, not just the word, for example hold a meeting.

tfn.s: All the marches passed off peacefully.
tfn.why: The text says the opposite: "Some marches led to clashes with police, injuries and arrests, prompting concerns about the treatment of young demonstrators."

tfn.s: The government offered several thousand extra replacement teachers.
tfn.why: The text says: "The government promised to provide 3,000 additional replacement teachers in the worst-affected areas."

tfn.s: The education minister met the student organisers.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not say whether the education minister met the student organisers.

tfn.s: Teaching unions think short-term contracts will not end the teacher shortage.
tfn.why: The text says the shortage "will not be cleared up by short-term contracts".

tfn.s: Police and campaigners agree that officers used too much force.
tfn.why: The text says students and campaigners accused police of too much force, while authorities said they had to respond to disorder.

focus.note: Many verbs go with particular nouns. Check the noun near the gap and ask which verb sounds natural with it.

the way things are at the moment

tfn.s: The writer suggests the campaign had gathered pace before Greta Thunberg arrived.
tfn.why: The text says the campaign "had already developed its own momentum".

tfn.s: The writer thinks the promise of extra replacement teachers will fully solve the problem.
tfn.why: The text says it "may alleviate immediate disruption" but cannot make up for sustained underinvestment.

tfn.s: Most of the injuries at the demonstrations were suffered by police officers.
tfn.why: The text mentions injuries and arrests but does not say who was hurt.

tfn.s: Campaigners and authorities disagree about the cause of the violence at some demonstrations.
tfn.why: Campaigners accuse officers of excessive force, while authorities point to incidents of violence.

tfn.s: Ministers who accept the students' case in principle but withhold funds are likely to end the dispute.
tfn.why: The text says such ministers "are unlikely to satisfy anyone for long".

focus.note: Look for fixed or semi-fixed expressions. If you change one word, the whole phrase may sound wrong.

speak.title: Role-play: the school march
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: Your teenage son or daughter wants to miss school on Friday to join a march about school buildings. You understand the problem, but you're worried. Ask at least two questions before you decide.

b.text: You want to join a student march on Friday. Explain why it matters, answer your parent's worries and suggest a plan that makes it safe.

phrases: I'd like to join the march on Friday.
It's not just about me, it's about everyone.
What if things get out of hand?
Could we agree on a compromise?
I'll catch up on the lesson at the weekend.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: did the parent agree, and what condition did they set?
